    <p>Kolkata is often called the <strong>Biryani Capital of Eastern India</strong>, and for good reason. The city has developed its own unique style of biryani, famous for fragrant long-grain rice, subtle spices, tender meat, and the iconic potato that has become an inseparable part of Kolkata biryani. While legendary restaurants like Arsalan, Aminia, Shiraz, and Royal Indian Hotel dominate the premium segment, there is another name that has quietly become a favorite among students, office workers, and budget-conscious food lovers—<strong>Shimla Biryani</strong>.</p><p>Over the years, Shimla Biryani has earned a reputation for serving affordable biryani without compromising too much on taste or quantity. With several outlets spread across Kolkata, it has become one of the city's most accessible biryani chains. But does it really deserve the popularity it enjoys? Is it worth visiting when there are so many biryani options available in Kolkata?</p><p>In this detailed review, we'll explore everything about Shimla Biryani—from its food quality and ambience to pricing, service, cleanliness, and overall value for money.</p><h2><strong>About Shimla Biryani</strong></h2><p>Shimla Biryani is a Kolkata-based restaurant chain specializing in Mughlai and North Indian cuisine. Since its establishment in <strong>2013</strong>, the brand has focused on a simple philosophy:</p><p><strong>Serve filling, tasty biryani at prices almost everyone can afford.</strong></p><p>Instead of investing heavily in luxury interiors or premium dining experiences, Shimla Biryani concentrates on what matters most to its customers—good food at reasonable prices.</p><p>Today, the restaurant operates multiple outlets across Kolkata and continues to attract thousands of customers every day.</p><h3><strong>Quick Information</strong></h3><ul><li><strong>Cuisine:</strong> Mughlai, North Indian, Biryani</li><li><strong>Founded:</strong> 2013</li><li><strong>Best For:</strong> Budget dining, takeaway, quick meals</li><li><strong>Average Cost for Two:</strong> ₹200–₹400</li><li><strong>Dining Style:</strong> Casual</li><li><strong>Delivery:</strong> Available through major food delivery platforms</li></ul><p> </p><h2><strong>First Impressions</strong></h2><p>Walking into a Shimla Biryani outlet, one thing becomes immediately clear—this is not a luxury restaurant.</p><p>Instead, the restaurant offers a practical and functional environment where customers can quickly order, eat, and leave.</p><p>You'll usually notice:</p><ul><li>Bright lighting</li><li>Simple furniture</li><li>Limited seating</li><li>Fast-moving crowd</li><li>Busy takeaway counters</li></ul><p>During lunch hours and evenings, many outlets remain packed with customers collecting takeaway orders.</p><p>If you're expecting elegant décor or a fine dining experience, Shimla Biryani isn't the place for you.</p><p>But if your only priority is delicious biryani at a reasonable price, you'll probably feel right at home.</p><p> </p><h2><strong>Ambience & Dining Experience</strong></h2><p><strong>Rating: 3.5/5</strong></p><p>The ambience is basic but functional.</p><h3><strong>Positives</strong></h3><ul><li>Clean     <p>Kolkata is often called the Biryani Capital of Eastern India, known for its subtle spices, fragrant long-grain rice, tender meat, and the iconic potato that defines its unique biryani style. Among the many legendary names that have shaped this culinary identity, Aminia stands as one of the oldest and most respected Mughlai restaurants in the city. Alongside iconic names like Arsalan, Shiraz, and Royal Indian Hotel, Aminia has built a reputation that spans generations.</p><p>For decades, Aminia has been synonymous with authentic Mughlai flavors, rich gravies, and consistently satisfying biryani. With multiple outlets across Kolkata, it continues to attract families, tourists, and loyal food lovers.
